articles.title: Mike Tomlin’s Patriots warning takes a serious turn after Mike Vrabel’s controversial comments leave more questions than answers
articles.summary: Mike Tomlin has raised concerns about what could be happening inside the New England Patriots after their 35-10 loss to the Detroit Lions in Munich on
articles.body: Mike Tomlin has raised concerns about what could be happening inside the New England Patriots after their 35-10 loss to the Detroit Lions in Munich on Sunday, November 15. The former Pittsburgh Steelers coach was more troubled by Mike Vrabel’s postgame comments than the result itself, as the Patriots head coach spoke about players who complain instead of helping the team win. Tomlin now wonders if there is a bigger problem within New England.Mike Tomlin questions Mike Vrabel’s comments about Patriots players after Lions defeatThe Patriots had a difficult afternoon in Germany, losing 35-10 to the Lions while also dealing with injuries to quarterback Drake Maye and wide receiver A.J. Brown. However, it was Vrabel’s words after the game that caught Tomlin’s attention during NBC’s Football Night in America.Speaking about the importance of helping the team, Vrabel said, “Winners figure out ways to help the team win. They don’t b***h and complain, they try to find ways to help the team.”When reporters asked whether he was suggesting that his own players were complaining, Vrabel tried to explain what he meant. He said he was speaking about winners in general and wanted his team to have the right mindset.Tomlin, however, was not fully convinced by the explanation. He said the Patriots had faced several challenges this season, but the coach’s choice of words made him question whether something else was happening within the team.“What alarms me is what Coach just said there. I don’t know who he was speaking to, or what he was referring to, but certainly, there’s probably some fire along with that smoke,” Tomlin said.He added, “I wasn’t this concerned, to be quite honest with you, until I heard his postgame. And it makes me lean in and wonder what’s going on behind the scenes.”Tomlin’s concern was not a claim that there was a confirmed dispute between Vrabel and his players. Rather, he wanted to understand why the Patriots coach felt the need to make such a statement after the defeat.Drake Maye and A.J. Brown injuries add to Mike Vrabel’s problems as Patriots enter bye weekThe defeat was made worse by the loss of two important offensive players. Maye suffered an ankle injury in the first quarter after being sacked by Detroit Lions defensive end Aidan Hutchinson. He left the field and did not return, forcing backup quarterback Tommy DeVito to take over.DeVito struggled to make an impact, completing 12 of 24 passes for 81 yards, one touchdown and one interception. With Maye’s injury still needing further tests, New England faces questions about who will lead its offense when the team returns from its bye week.A.J. Brown also failed to finish the game after suffering a hamstring injury in the second half. It was another setback for the wide receiver, who had already missed two games with ankle and knee problems before returning against Detroit. According to Boston.com, Vrabel said the team would check the severity of both injuries after returning home.There was another incident that brought attention to Vrabel after the defeat. The Patriots coach was seen spending time with fans at Augustiner Stammhaus, a German beer hall, just hours after the loss. Videos of him enjoying the evening spread online and drew criticism from some Patriots fans in the United States.New England now enters its bye week with a 5-5 record and sits second in the AFC East. The team is still in the playoff race, but its recent results and injury problems have made the remaining games more important. The Patriots have also lost three of their last four games, leaving Vrabel with several issues to address before their next matchup.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.
